questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How driverless cars can communicate with people
Why driverless cars are cheaper than normal taxis
How to become a licensed taxi driver in London
Why cyclists cause more accidents than drivers
questions.why: They discuss how driverless cars will interact with pedestrians, runners and cyclists, and the tech to help.

questions.q: What problem does Professor Stephen Brewster describe?
options: Driverless cars drive far too slowly in busy cities
Pedestrians can't see driverless cars at night
With no driver, you can't agree by eye contact
Driverless cars can't recognise traffic lights
questions.why: He says there's no person in the driving seat, so how do you negotiate who is going to go?

questions.q: How does Phil say he would feel crossing the road in front of a robotaxi?
options: Completely relaxed, because the cars are safe
A bit nervous, so he might let it pass first
Excited to try something new and modern
Angry that there is nobody in the driving seat
questions.why: Phil says he'd be a little nervous and might wait for it to go and walk behind it.

questions.q: What does Pippa think will happen over time?
options: People will stop crossing roads on foot at all
Driverless cars will be banned in most cities
Accidents will increase every year from now on
People will get used to the cars and adapt
questions.why: She thinks as we get more used to these technologies, we'll learn how to deal with them and when to cross.

questions.q: Which two kinds of signals did Stephen Brewster's team test?
options: Loud horns and brightly flashing headlights
Recorded voice messages and phone alerts
Moving images and fixed coloured light rings
Hand signals from robots and new road signs
questions.why: He says they tested animations and fixed, coloured light rings.

questions.q: Why did the animations not work well for runners and cyclists?
options: They move fast and only have time for a glance
The animations were too small and dark to see
They don't pay any attention to cars at all
The animations only worked well in the dark
questions.why: He says runners and cyclists have less time to decide, and with a quick glance you don't see the animation.

questions.q: Why does Pippa mention hand waving?
options: To explain how drivers usually say hello
To show that waving is illegal in some countries
To suggest that cars should have robot hands
To show body language differs between cultures
questions.why: She says waving can mean 'please proceed' in one culture but 'thank you' in another.

questions.q: According to Ammar Al-Taie, why is South Korea well suited to driverless cars?
options: Its roads are much wider than roads in the UK
People rarely cross where it isn't allowed
Most people there already own electric cars
It has far fewer cyclists than other countries
questions.why: He says jaywalking is illegal in South Korea, whereas in the UK people jaywalk a lot.
